rendered: The solvent with the strongest hydrogen bonding in the paper is water. Its Hansen hydrogen-bonding parameter is δH =[1] 42.3 MPa^1/2[2] (shown in the figure of δH values for PVDF and the solvents diethylene glycol, EG, glycerol and water). EG is next with a high δH, and glycerol and diethylene glycol are also high (values of[3] 29.3[4] and 20.7[5] MPa^1/2, respectively). Water is not used for delamination because the aluminum foil corrodes: lithium leaching from the NMC cathode makes the water solution basic, and the corroded aluminum then contaminates the NMC particles by forming Al(OH)3 precipitates on the cathode surfaces.[6][7][8][9] So the reason is chemical (aluminum corrosion and contamination of the cathode), not a lack of hydrogen bonding; EG was chosen instead because it also has a high δH and avoids this corrosion problem.
